summary: The note surveys how schools across the nation are embedding environmental sustainability into education and operations. It profiles specific school initiatives covering gardening, zero-waste recycling, green buildings, green transportation, solar power, community outreach, curriculum integration and teacher training. It closes by noting that impact is measured with qualitative and quantitative metrics and that the story is still unfolding.
one_line: Examples of schools nationwide pioneering sustainability through gardens, recycling, green buildings, solar power, biking, curriculum and teacher training.
key_facts: Maplewood Elementary launched its Sprout-to-Plate program in fall 2023 under principal Kristina Jameson; students grow crops and eat them in school lunches.
The Maplewood Greenhouse opened on November 12th; it is student-managed and runs on rainwater collection and solar power.
Lincoln High School's 'Green Ambassadors', led by senior Adam Nguyen, launched a school-wide recycling and composting program on September 15th.
Lincoln High School aims to redirect 80% of school waste from landfills by the end of the academic year.
Lincoln's 'Compost Club' turns food scraps into nutrient-rich soil for the school gardens.
Riverside Academy's Principal Michael Davidson unveiled a new sustainable library on September 20th with natural lighting, passive solar heating and a roof garden.
Riverside facilities manager Lila Torres calls the green buildings "living lessons in sustainability".
Sunset Middle's 'Bike-to-School' program, coordinated by Roger Chen and launched October 1st, led to a tripling of students cycling to school.
Sunset Middle also runs a 'Walking School Bus' where groups of students walk to school with adult supervision.
Roosevelt High School installed photovoltaic solar panels on September 30th, driven by science teacher David Kim; they generate 50% of the school's electricity.
Jefferson Elementary hosted its first annual Green Fair on November 20th to engage students and parents in sustainable living.
East Marlin High School introduced its 'Sustainable Futures' program on September 1st, using project-based learning with a year-end showcase.
The Summer Green Institute held its first session in July 2024 to train educators from varying districts in teaching sustainability; Samantha Barrett is cited as a champion.
